VITTER LLC; JOHNSON FOODS, LLC; LP * IND., LLC; CAG HOLDINGS, LLC; * MAGISTRATE DONNA PHILLIPS RMH HOLDINGS, INC.; ABC * CURRAULT INSURANCE COMPANY and John * Does 1-4, * * Defendants. DEFENDANTS’ MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT Defendants LP Ind., LLC; CAG Holdings, LLC; RMH Holdings, Inc.; Martian Sales, Inc.; Johnson Foods, LLC; JOpen, LLC; Nuza, LLC; Calibre Manufacturing, LLC; FMK Group, Inc.; PNW Holdings, LLC; CC US Holdings, LLC; Peyton Palaio; Mark Jennings; David Gabbay; and Mark Reilly (collectively “Defendants”) pursuant to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 56, respectfully move this Honorable Court for summary judgment on all claims asserted against them should the Court deny Defendants’ pending Motion to Dismiss, for the reasons stated in the attached Memorandum in Support of Defendants’ Motion for Summary Judgment.1 1 All Defendants have moved to dismiss the Complaint under Rule 12(b)(6). All Defendants other than JOpen have moved to dismiss the Third Amended Complaint under Rule 12(b)(2) for lack of personal jurisdiction. Dkt. 122. The Court must find that it has personal jurisdiction over each defendant before it makes any decision on the merits. Sinochem Int'l Co. v. Malaysia Int'l Shipping Corp., 549 U.S. 422, 430, 127 S.Ct. 1184, 167 L.Ed.2d 15 (2007). Other than JOpen, each Defendants’ request for summary judgment is contingent upon the Court first finding personal jurisdiction over them.
